issues.legal_issue: Whether an agreement and the parties’ conduct created a genuine partnership for purposes of registering a firm for agricultural income-tax assessment.
material_facts: The estate was owned by one brother, and before the agreement the other brother managed it as his agent.

The agreement described the estate as the firm’s capital but barred the managing brother from contributing to, encumbering, or otherwise dealing with it, and provided that the estate would return to its owner on dissolution.
The agreement required the managing brother to work and maintain accounts, while the owner could inspect the accounts and approve expenditure estimates; it did not require the owner to work.
The managing brother’s remuneration depended on profits, and the agreement made no provision for sharing losses.

After the agreement, the claim for a change of status was made without a corresponding change in the estate’s management or accounting records; the owner also continued to claim the estate’s expenses and losses.
The tax authorities refused to register the firm, and the High Court upheld that refusal.
issues.conclusion: The agreement, considered together with the parties’ conduct, did not create a partnership; the refusal to register the firm was upheld and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 6 of the Partnership Act, whether persons form a partnership depends on their real relationship as shown by all relevant facts taken together. Sharing profits, or receiving remuneration contingent on profits, does not by itself establish partnership, since a servant may be remunerated in that way. The court considered In re Ambalal Sarabhai and Raghunandan Nanu Kothare v. Hormasji Bezonjee Bamjee, noting that the construction of documents depends on their circumstances and that the facts there differed. It also considered Robinson v. Ashton concerning property credited as partnership capital, but held that the estate in this case had not become partnership capital. Registration under section 26 of the Coorg Agricultural Income-tax Act depended on the existence of a firm.

rule.if: partnership_tax_registration_proceeding and prior_agency_relationship and continued_owner_control and purported_partner_lacked_asset_interest and purported_partner_could_not_contribute_or_encumber_asset and owner_approved_expenditure and owner_could_inspect_accounts and no_loss_sharing_term and unchanged_management_or_accounts_after_agreement

predicates.partnership_tax_registration_proceeding: The dispute arose in a proceeding seeking tax registration of a purported firm.
predicates.prior_agency_relationship: Before the agreement, one person managed the business or property as the other person’s agent.
predicates.continued_owner_control: The owner retained control over the business, including approval of expenditure, while the other person had no comparable management authority.
predicates.purported_partner_lacked_asset_interest: The agreement denied the purported partner an interest in the principal asset and provided for its return to the owner on dissolution.
predicates.purported_partner_could_not_contribute_o: The agreement barred the purported partner from contributing to, encumbering, or otherwise dealing with the principal asset.
predicates.owner_approved_expenditure: The agreement required the owner to approve expenditure estimates prepared by the purported partner.
predicates.owner_could_inspect_accounts: The agreement allowed the owner to inspect the accounts maintained by the purported partner and ask questions about them.
predicates.no_loss_sharing_term: The agreement made no provision for the purported partners to share losses.
predicates.unchanged_management_or_accounts_after_a: After the agreement, the parties’ management practices or accounting records did not show a change consistent with the claimed new relationship.

issues.definition: When a tax-registration dispute involves a prior agency relationship and the owner retains control and the principal asset, while the agreement and subsequent conduct lack features of shared partnership responsibility, the agreement did not create a partnership.
